notes: Both coders found the same three university-layer documents (Provost faculty page, Provost student page, ITS AI and Acceptable Use) and set the same stance on each (delegates, delegates, permit); neither found a school or computing policy. Main disagreements: (1) phase for general principles and rules applied at the moment of use (acceptable-use page: A general, B during-work), resolved as during-work when the sentence is about using AI and general for default-stance statements in the sample syllabus tiers; (2) actor for the data-protection rule on the faculty page (A all, B instructor), resolved as instructor because the page addresses faculty, and for the student page's 'NAU encourages the responsible use' sentence (student); (3) policy_type splits: sample-statement offer (P63 vs P05, kept P63 with fit_note), chatbot-exploration assignment (P12 vs P35, kept P12), 'Treat AI as a collaborator, not a replacement' (P32 vs P45, kept P32 since no existing-rules reference); (4) modality: detector fact (should vs informs, informs) and 'Be cognizant ... not definitive evidence' (must-not vs should-not, should-not); (5) unit_stance, the largest source of disagreement (about 18 units): resolved by whether the single sentence takes a position on AI use (equity, evidence and compliance duties are neutral; bans on AI-produced final work are prohibit; narrow listed uses are restrict). Only-A units (2) were real statements and kept: 'effective companion rather than relying on it entirely' and the Disability Resource office referral. Only-B unit (1) kept: the pointer to the service catalog for permitted data levels per approved tool. Topic codes: A used some labels outside the corpus vocabulary, so B's topic codes were adopted for matched units. new_types empty on both sides.
